front.title: Skill Design Specification (SDS): A Composability, Safety, and Interoperability Layer for Agent Skills

abstract.t: The Agent Skills format defines how a single skill is packaged (a directory, a SKILL.md file, optional scripts/, references/, and assets/ subdirectories) so that a model can discover and load it. It is silent on how a family of skills, authored over time by possibly different people, should relate to one another so that the family behaves as one coherent, composable system rather than a directory of unrelated documents that happen to share a container format. This document specifies that additional layer, top to bottom: a conceptual model of a skill as a typed, effectful function (Part 0); the layout, registry, versioning, and governance of a skill family (Part I); the reference kit every family ships and the rules for extending it (Part II); and the complete anatomy of a single conforming skill package, from frontmatter to fixtures (Part III). Every normative rule carries a permanent identifier and a conformance tag stating whether a linter checks it, a human reviews it, or it is advisory. It is written to be domain-independent; a companion document applies it to a software-development skill catalog as a worked example.

section.name: Purpose and Scope
section.t: This specification governs the design of a Skill Family: two or more skills intended to be authored, versioned, and used together, potentially chained so that one skill's output becomes another's input. It applies regardless of domain; domain-specific choices made under this specification's rules are recorded in a domain-specific companion document, not here.
This document does not specify:

ul.li: any particular domain's catalog of skills (see );
runtime enforcement mechanisms outside the skill author's control (a given host's tool-approval implementation is out of scope, though depends on one existing).

section.name: Relationship to the Base Spec
section.t: The Base Spec fixes the physical packaging of a single skill: a directory named identically to the skill's name, containing a required SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name, description, optional license, compatibility, metadata, and experimental allowed-tools) followed by Markdown instructions, and optional scripts/, references/, and assets/ directories. It also fixes progressive disclosure: metadata (~100 tokens) is always resident, the SKILL.md body (recommended under 5,000 tokens and under 500 lines) loads only once a skill is activated, and files under scripts/, references/, or assets/ load only on demand.

Every requirement in this document is expressed as additional structure inside that envelope: fixed sections within the SKILL.md body, additional key/value pairs inside the Base Spec's free-form metadata map, constraints on the contents of allowed-tools, and one family-level extension directory, evals/, that hosts ignore. This document defines no new frontmatter keys at the top level. Shape schemas and the kit live outside any skill package, so a host loading a single skill never sees them; a skill therefore cites a shape by name first and by path second.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: a set of skills governed by one instance of this specification, sharing one Shape Registry (), one kit (), and one Family Registry File ().
the directory that contains kit/, skills/, and docs/. All root-relative paths in this document resolve against the family root. The family root is not necessarily the version-control toplevel.
a skill whose most severe declared effect is "external-read-only" or lower on the Effect Ladder (). Produces an artifact; performs no effect outside itself.
a skill whose most severe declared effect is "local-write" or higher. Performs an effect in addition to, or instead of, producing an artifact.
a named, versioned, machine-checkable structural type that an artifact conforms to ().
one unit of a skill's Procedure, drawn from the closed vocabulary in .
one level of the six-level Effect Ladder.
a skill's priority within its family: pillar or situational.

section.name: Notational Conventions
section.t: Pipeline composition is written left to right with an arrow: A -> B means "the output of A is the input to B." Optional stages are bracketed: [Confirm]; a conditional pair is parenthesized: (Confirm -> Act). A skill's overall type is written as shown below.

section.name: Rule Identifiers and Conformance Tags
section.t: Every normative rule in this document is stated as its own paragraph headed by a permanent identifier of the form SDS-P-NNN, where P is C (core model, Part 0), F (family, Part I), K (kit, Part II), or S (skill anatomy, Part III). Identifiers are never reused; a withdrawn rule remains listed as withdrawn. Each rule also carries a requirement level (MUST, SHOULD, or MAY) and exactly one conformance tag:

dl.dd: checked by the family's linter (). A MUST+MACHINE failure is an error; SHOULD+MACHINE is a warning; MAY+MACHINE is informational.
requires human judgment; the linter prints these as a checklist, never as failures.
guidance; never a conformance failure.

section.t: lists every rule with its identifier, slug, section, level, and tag; the linter's own rule table MUST match it ().

section.name: Document Map
section.t: Part 0 ( through ) is the conceptual model: what a skill is, how its procedure is structured, how skills exchange artifacts, and how effects are governed. Part I () is the family and repository layer. Part II () is the reference kit every family ships. Part III () is the complete anatomy of one skill package. Readers building a skill start at Part III and follow its cross-references back into Part 0 for rationale.

section.name: A Skill as a Function
section.t: SDS-C-001 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill MUST declare five parts:

dl.dd: the condition of activation — the Base Spec's description plus an explicit statement of when the skill does not apply ().
the skill's parameters, each marked REQUIRED or OPTIONAL with a stated default ().
the ordered body, built from the stage grammar ().
the skill's declared effect contract ().
a Result — a conforming success Shape, or one of a finite, declared set of failure shapes ().

section.t: This model lets two independently-authored skills be reasoned about the same way two functions in a typed codebase are: by their signature, not by reading their full implementation.

section.name: Command-Query Separation
section.t: SDS-C-002 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill MUST obey Command-Query Separation : it is either a Query Skill (produces information, no side effect) or a Command Skill (produces an effect; any information it also returns is a report of that effect, not an independent analytical artifact). A skill that both performs a mutating effect and produces a materially independent analytical artifact MUST be split into a Query Skill feeding a Command Skill via the pipe composition rule in .

section.name: Purity, Referential Transparency, and Idempotence
section.t: SDS-C-003 (MUST, REVIEW) A Query Skill's Procedure is pure with respect to its declared Inputs: given the same Inputs and no undeclared ambient state (the current date, network state not listed as an Input, files not listed as an Input), it MUST produce the same Output. This is a hermeticity requirement on the Gather stage: a Query Skill's Gather stage MUST read only what its Inputs declaration lists. A skill satisfying this is referentially transparent: any invocation MAY be replaced, anywhere in a pipeline, by its previously-computed Output for the same Inputs. Referential transparency is the single property that licenses caching, reordering (), and parallel execution.

SDS-C-004 (MAY, ADVISORY) metadata.idempotent declares the weaker property "safe to re-call with identical arguments," matching the Model Context Protocol's idempotentHint . It does not declare, and does not trigger, the fixed-point composition law (); a Command Skill can be idempotent in this sense (opening an already-open PR is a no-op) without being pure.

section.name: Totality
section.t: SDS-C-005 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill's declared behavior MUST be total over its declared Input domain: for every input satisfying its stated preconditions, including boundary cases (empty input, a single item, the maximum stated size, malformed-but-precondition-satisfying input), the skill MUST have a defined, non-crashing Output — either a success Shape or a declared failure Shape. Undefined behavior on a precondition-satisfying input is a specification defect, not an implementation gap.

section.name: Stage Vocabulary
section.t: SDS-C-010 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill's Procedure MUST be expressed using only the following stage vocabulary, presented as SKILL.md subheadings in the order given (machine check: ).

tr.td: Collect raw material. Touches only inputs declared in .
Narrow gathered material to what is relevant.
Interpret gathered material against a rubric; the primary locus of model judgment.
Assign a label or severity to each analyzed item.
Choose or propose among options; produces a decision-shaped artifact.
Combine analyzed material into one artifact.
Check a claim or artifact against fixed criteria.
Produce new content in a target format from existing content.
Change state outside the skill's own output artifact. Command Skills only.
Send information to an audience outside the artifact itself.
Write the artifact to its declared location.
Invoke another skill, subagent, or external tool for a sub-task.

section.name: Canonical Pipelines
section.t: SDS-C-011 (MUST, REVIEW) A Query Skill's Procedure MUST reduce to the Query pipeline. Filter and Classify are optional and MAY be omitted entirely.

SDS-C-012 (MUST, REVIEW) A Command Skill's Procedure MUST reduce to the Command pipeline. The parenthesized Confirm/Act pair is conditional: it MAY be skipped on an invocation only by a branch declared in Decide, per ; both headings are retained. Communicate and Persist headings are always present ().
section.artwork:
Query pipeline (a Query Skill):
Gather -> [Filter] -> Analyze -> [Classify] -> Synthesize
Command pipeline (a Command Skill):
Gather -> Analyze -> Decide -> (Confirm -> Act) -> [Communicate] -> [Persist]
section.t: SDS-C-013 (MUST, REVIEW) Nothing MAY follow Synthesize in a Query pipeline that touches state outside the produced artifact; a Procedure that does so is, by definition, a Command Skill and MUST be labeled and gated as one.

section.name: Composition Semantics
section.t: SDS-C-014 (MUST, REVIEW) Stage composition within a Procedure, and skill composition within a pipeline, follows railway-oriented composition : every stage returns a success value or a failure value. A failure at any stage MUST short-circuit every subsequent stage and proceed directly to the declared failure Output (). A Procedure or orchestrator MUST NOT require per-stage bespoke "what if the prior stage failed" logic.

section.name: Composition Laws
section.t: The following laws hold for a Query Skill's Procedure and are checked by the eval table ().

SDS-C-015 (MUST, REVIEW) Identity. Composing a skill with the identity transform MUST leave its behavior unchanged in either order. An empty-result Output () is the identity element of its Shape and MUST be handled by downstream consumers via their ordinary code path.

SDS-C-016 (MUST, REVIEW) Associativity. For composable stages f, g, h: (f -> g) -> h MUST equal f -> (g -> h). Lossy reduction ("keep only the top N") MUST occur only once, at the final Synthesize stage; intermediate combination MUST be lossless.

SDS-C-017 (MUST, REVIEW) Fixed point. Where a skill's shape-out equals its shape-in and both name a registered Shape, applying the skill to its own Output a second time MUST produce no further change. freeform paired with freeform does not qualify: freeform is the declared absence of structure, not a structure an output can be fed back into. metadata.idempotent does not trigger this law (). Machine check: .

SDS-C-018 (MUST, REVIEW) Map fusion. Where a skill is applied across a collection, map(f) -> map(g) MUST equal map(f -> g). Where it does not, the two stages have a hidden dependency and MUST NOT be fused into a single parallel pass.

section.name: Fail-Fast Validation
section.t: SDS-C-019 (MUST, REVIEW) A Procedure MUST validate every stated precondition as its first action, before Gather proceeds. A violation MUST produce an immediate, specific failure naming the unmet precondition, mapped to a declared @throws code; it MUST NOT be discovered partway through Analyze or later.

section.name: Termination Requirements
section.t: SDS-C-020 (MUST, REVIEW) Any stage that iterates internally MUST declare an explicit termination condition: a convergence check or a stated maximum number of iterations. Open-ended iteration with no declared termination condition is nonconformant.

section.name: The Shape Registry
section.t: Skills compose by agreeing on the structure of what they exchange, never by one skill invoking another directly. Each family maintains a Shape Registry: the set of kit/shapes/<name>.schema.json files ().
SDS-C-030 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill's @returns and @requires MUST name a registered Shape, or explicitly declare freeform where no structural contract is offered. Machine checks: , .

section.name: The Standards-First Rule
section.t: SDS-C-031 (MUST, REVIEW) Before registering a new Shape, the family MUST check whether an established external interchange format already exists for that category of artifact in the family's domain, and adopt or wrap it rather than defining a competing bespoke structure. Illustrative software-development examples: SARIF for finding-style results, the OSV schema for vulnerability records, SPDX or CycloneDX for dependency manifests, MADR for decision records, the C4 model for architecture diagrams, Diataxis for documentation quadrants, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for observability fields, the Twelve-Factor App rubric for environment checks, and Conventional Commits with Keep a Changelog for release-note generation. Each registered Shape has a machine-checkable JSON Schema ().

section.name: The Null Object Requirement
section.t: SDS-C-033 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill whose Analyze/Classify stage finds nothing MUST still produce a fully well-formed, schema-valid instance of its declared Shape with zero entries — never null, an empty string, an omitted file, or a distinct "nothing found" format (the Null Object pattern ).

section.name: Immutability and Supersession
section.t: SDS-C-034 (SHOULD, REVIEW) Once persisted, an artifact instance SHOULD be treated as immutable. Where a later invocation would otherwise update a decision- or plan-shaped artifact, it MUST persist a new, dated instance referencing the instance it supersedes (the superseded by convention established by MADR ).

section.name: The Effect Ladder
section.t: SDS-C-040 (MUST, REVIEW) Each skill MUST declare, in metadata.effect-tier, the single highest rung its Procedure reaches on the following ordered ladder.

ol.li: domain-read-only (reads a closed, predictable domain, e.g. version-controlled repository history)
external-read-only (reads an open-world external system: a network API, a live service)
local-write (writes only the skill's own declared output location)
shared-write (writes to, or notifies, something other skills, people, or systems depend on)
irreversible (an effect that cannot be undone by a compensating action, or whose undo is itself irreversible)

section.t: SDS-C-041 (MUST, REVIEW) Rungs 1 through 3 define a Query Skill; rungs 4 through 6 define a Command Skill. A skill at rung 5 or 6 MUST include a Confirm stage. Machine check: .

section.name: Relationship to MCP Tool Annotations
section.t: SDS-C-042 (SHOULD, ADVISORY) Where a skill is exposed as, or invokes, a Model Context Protocol tool, its rung SHOULD be reflected in that tool's annotations : readOnlyHint for rungs 1-3, destructiveHint for rung 6, idempotentHint for the metadata.idempotent declaration, and openWorldHint for rung 3 or any rung reached via an external system.

section.name: Permission Scoping
section.t: SDS-C-043 (MUST, REVIEW) allowed-tools is scoped by rung, not by kind. Any skill whose Procedure reaches rung 2 or above and invokes any tool or bundled script MUST declare a narrow scope; operations that would place the skill at rung 5 or 6 MUST NOT appear in it under any kind, so that mis-scoping cannot suppress the host's own approval mechanism. Machine checks: through .

section.name: Confirmation Gates
section.t: SDS-C-044 (MUST, REVIEW) A Confirm stage functions as middleware in front of Act: it MUST run on every invocation that reaches an Act at rung 5 or above, MUST NOT be skipped because an equivalent confirmation was granted earlier in the session, and MUST state concretely what specific effect is about to occur.

section.name: Compensating Actions
section.t: SDS-C-045 (MUST, REVIEW) Each mutating step of an Act stage MUST have a declared compensating action, to be taken if a later step in the same sequence fails (the saga pattern ). Where none exists, the step MUST say so and be sequenced last.

section.name: Check-Before-Act and Checkpointing
section.t: SDS-C-046 (MUST, REVIEW) Every mutating step MUST verify current state before mutating and MUST skip as an explicit no-op when the effect is already applied, so that re-invocation after an interruption is safe rather than duplicative.

SDS-C-047 (MUST, REVIEW) A Command Skill MUST persist a two-phase checkpoint for each mutating step, written before the step and updated after it, so that resumption after an interruption is well-defined. The record format and location are specified in ; machine check: .

section.name: Trust Model for Declared Hints
section.t: SDS-C-048 (MUST, ADVISORY) Effect Ladder rungs, MCP annotations, and allowed-tools scopes are declared hints. A host MUST NOT treat a skill's own declaration as the sole safety control; declared risk, permission scoping, and host-level approval are independently redundant controls (defense in depth), per the caution that annotation hints are untrusted unless sourced from a trusted party .

section.name: Precondition/Postcondition Notation
section.t: SDS-C-050 (MUST, REVIEW) Following Design by Contract , every skill MUST state @requires (preconditions as testable assertions), @returns (the guarantee about a successful Output, naming a Shape), and @throws (every declared failure mode, exhaustive with respect to ). Machine check: .
SDS-C-051 (MUST, REVIEW) Each precondition MUST be marked REQUIRED or OPTIONAL with a stated default. Machine check: .
SDS-C-052 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill declaring more than five REQUIRED inputs MUST be split into narrower skills or take one bundled Shape instead (the long-parameter-list smell). Machine check: .

section.name: The Result Type and Failure Modes
section.t: A skill's Output is modeled as shown below.

SDS-C-053 (MUST, REVIEW) A Failure value MUST preserve the causal chain of what was being attempted at each level, in the style of wrapped errors in idiomatic Go ("could not produce X: could not read Y: reason"), rather than surfacing only the innermost cause or only a generic top-level message.

section.name: Substitutability
section.t: SDS-C-054 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill published as a replacement for another MUST satisfy the Liskov Substitution Principle against every declared consumer of the original: preconditions no stronger, postconditions no weaker. A version increment alone does not establish substitutability; it MUST be verified against declared consumers.

section.name: Functional Core, Imperative Shell
section.t: SDS-C-060 (SHOULD, REVIEW) An orchestrating Command Skill SHOULD contain no Analyze, Classify, or Decide logic of its own ; that reasoning belongs in a Query Skill it invokes via a Delegate stage. The orchestrator's own Procedure reduces to: delegate for a decision artifact, Confirm, Act.

section.name: Specialization via Injection
section.t: SDS-C-061 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill MUST NOT be forked to specialize it for one context. Context-specific configuration MUST be supplied via assets/ or compatibility as an injected dependency , with the Procedure written against the abstract presence of that dependency.

section.name: Migration via the Strangler Fig Pattern
section.t: SDS-C-062 (MUST, REVIEW) Adoption of a new Shape, standard, or convention across an existing family MUST proceed incrementally : revised skills adopt it directly; an Adapter (a judgment-free translation script) bridges unmigrated output; the Adapter is retired once no unmigrated skill remains.

section.name: Consumer-Driven Contract Testing
section.t: SDS-C-063 (SHOULD, REVIEW) Where two skills are designed to chain, the eval suite SHOULD include a consumer-driven contract test : the producer is run for real and its actual Output validated against the consumer's declared @requires schema. Per-skill evals passing in isolation MUST NOT be treated as evidence that two skills chain correctly.

section.name: Layout
section.t: SDS-F-001 (MUST, MACHINE) The family root MUST contain kit/, skills/, and docs/.
SDS-F-002 (MUST, MACHINE) skills/ MUST contain only skill package directories, each holding a SKILL.md.

SDS-F-003 (MUST, REVIEW) The XML source of this specification under docs/superpowers/specs/ is authoritative; rendered .txt and .html files are derived and MUST be regenerated with xml2rfc in the same change that edits the XML.

section.name: The Family Registry File
section.t: SDS-F-010 (MUST, MACHINE) The canonical registry MUST be kit/registry/marketplace.json.
SDS-F-011 (MUST, MACHINE) The registry MUST validate against kit/registry/marketplace.schema.json.
SDS-F-012 (MUST, MACHINE) Each entry MUST carry name, description, version, effect-tier, tier, shape-out, and shape-in.
SDS-F-013 (MUST, MACHINE) Every skills/<name>/ MUST have exactly one entry, and the entry's version, effect-tier, tier, shape-out, and shape-in MUST equal the skill's frontmatter.
SDS-F-014 (MUST, REVIEW) Any human-facing index of the family's skills MUST be generated from the registry, never hand-maintained in parallel.
SDS-F-015 (MUST, MACHINE) An entry's status is planned or built. A built entry MUST have a corresponding skill directory; a planned entry need not; a skill directory without an entry is an error.
SDS-F-016 (SHOULD, MACHINE) An entry's description SHOULD equal the skill's frontmatter description after whitespace collapse.

section.name: Root Ignore Rules and Runtime State
section.t: SDS-F-020 (MUST, MACHINE) The family-root .gitignore MUST contain .skills-state/.
SDS-F-021 (MUST, MACHINE) No file under .skills-state/ MUST be tracked by version control; it is machine state for one run ().

section.name: Path Convention
section.t: SDS-F-030 (MUST, MACHINE) Every cross-reference to a file under kit/, skills/, or docs/ — in SKILL.md, eval files, scripts, templates, and kit guides — MUST be family-root-relative (e.g. kit/shapes/finding-list.schema.json). Parent-relative references (../) and bare shapes/, shared/, templates/, or registry/ references MUST NOT be used, and every referenced kit/ path MUST exist.

SDS-F-031 (MUST, MACHINE) Commands in SKILL.md and eval files run from the skill directory and use skill-relative paths (scripts/x.py, evals/fixtures/y); every such referenced path MUST exist, except generated fixtures (). A consumer-driven contract row () MAY run another skill's script by its family-root-relative path (skills/<other>/scripts/<file>, reached from the skill directory through the family root); such a token resolves against that skill and MUST exist there.
SDS-F-032 (MAY, ADVISORY) Tooling resolves root-relative paths by locating the family root (the parent of kit/), never by asking version control for its toplevel, which may be a different directory.

section.name: Versioning and Release
section.t: SDS-F-040 (MUST, MACHINE) metadata.version MUST be Semantic Versioning .
SDS-F-041 (MUST, REVIEW) A change to a registered Shape is MAJOR if it removes or narrows a field, MINOR if it adds an optional field, PATCH otherwise.

SDS-F-042 (MUST, MACHINE) The registry's top-level sds string MUST name the specification version the family conforms to (e.g. 1.0-draft). No metadata key is added for this; the seven-key set stays closed.
SDS-F-043 (MUST, REVIEW) A MAJOR change to a shared Shape MUST trigger a review of every skill declaring that Shape in shape-in or shape-out before release.
SDS-F-044 (MUST, REVIEW) Every revision of this specification MUST add an entry to .

section.name: Governance
section.t: SDS-F-050 (MUST, REVIEW) A change to this specification MUST consist of the XML edit, regenerated renderings, and — when a MACHINE rule is added, removed, or changed — the matching linter update in the same change.
SDS-F-051 (MUST, REVIEW) Rule identifiers MUST NOT be reused; a withdrawn rule remains in marked withdrawn.
SDS-F-052 (MUST, ADVISORY) Kit guides () are non-normative; where a guide and this specification conflict, the specification governs.

SDS-F-053 (SHOULD, REVIEW) Promotion of a skill from situational to pillar SHOULD require a numeric threshold over real invocations (an error-budget style criterion ) recorded under docs/, not a subjective judgment.

SDS-F-054 (SHOULD, ADVISORY) A family SHOULD run its validation gate () — the linter over every skill, the registry against its schema, generated files against the registry, and the eval runner () — in continuous integration on every push and pull request. The gate is offline by construction (), so the job needs no credential and mutates nothing.

section.name: Glossary
section.t: SDS-F-060 (MUST, MACHINE) A family MUST maintain exactly one glossary at kit/shared/glossary.md, fixing one canonical term per concept.

SDS-F-061 (SHOULD, MACHINE) A skill's headings, @requires bullets, @returns line, and description SHOULD NOT use a term the glossary lists under "do not use instead." A term that is part of a proper noun or an identifier is not a synonym for the family concept and is exempt: a product or command namespace (GitHub Projects, gh project), a capitalised name following another capitalised word (JSON Schema, OpenAPI Description), a hyphenated name (project-board-sync), or a backticked literal (`FORMAT JSON`). The linter applies a conservative single-word heuristic with exactly those exemptions; the reserved words tier, rung, gate, and checkpoint require human review.

section.name: Layout and Status
section.t: SDS-K-001 (MUST, MACHINE) kit/ MUST contain templates/, evals/TEMPLATE.eval.yaml, shapes/, shared/glossary.md, shared/gates/, shared/tool-profiles/, registry/, scripts/lint-skill.py, and scripts/run-evals.py.

SDS-K-002 (MUST, MACHINE) kit/HOW-TO-BUILD-A-SKILL.md and kit/PRIMITIVES.md are non-normative guides and MUST open with a banner stating so and naming this specification; their sections cite rule identifiers.

section.name: Templates
section.t: SDS-K-010 (MUST, MACHINE) The kit ships one Query template and one Command template under kit/templates/; their H2 and H3 heading order MUST equal the normative order in .

section.name: Shapes: Adding One
section.t: SDS-K-020 (MUST, MACHINE) A registered Shape is a file kit/shapes/<name>.schema.json that is JSON Schema draft 2020-12, whose title equals <name> and whose $id is https://skills.local/shapes/<name>.schema.json.
SDS-K-021 (MUST, REVIEW) A new Shape MUST carry a Standards-First justification in its description () and a zero-entry instance that validates ().
SDS-K-022 (SHOULD, REVIEW) A Shape that introduces a term SHOULD add a glossary row.

SDS-K-023 (SHOULD, REVIEW) A family SHOULD carry a machine check that each registered Shape remains backward compatible with its copy at the last tagged release: a frozen recording of every kit/shapes/<name>.schema.json at the tag, diffed against the current file by a skill or script that reports the changes able to reject a previously valid instance. A break found this way is the MAJOR change of and requires the review that rule names. In this family the check is json-schema-compat-check's contract-with-family-shapes eval row.

section.name: Gates: Adding One
section.t: SDS-K-030 (MUST, MACHINE) A gate is a file kit/shared/gates/<level>.md containing the fields What, Why, and either Reversible or Compensating action.
SDS-K-031 (MUST, REVIEW) Each gate MUST map to exactly one rung and be cited from .

section.name: Tool Profiles: Adding One
section.t: SDS-K-040 (MUST, MACHINE) A tool profile is a file kit/shared/tool-profiles/<name>.yaml with name, effect-tier (a rung), allowed-tools (a list), and notes.

SDS-K-041 (MUST, MACHINE) No profile entry MUST be a rung-5 or rung-6 operation. The family denylist is: gh pr merge, git push, git merge, git rebase, git reset, git branch -D / -d, gh release create, gh repo delete, gh issue close, gh pr close, gh api -X POST|PATCH|PUT|DELETE, rm -rf, git clean (forbidden always); and gh pr create, gh pr edit, gh pr comment, gh issue create, git commit, git add (forbidden in any profile below rung 5).
SDS-K-042 (MUST, MACHINE) No profile entry MUST be a bare interpreter or wildcard: Bash(*), Bash(python3:*), Bash(sh:*), Bash(bash:*), Bash(node:*), or bare Bash.

SDS-K-043 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Skills SHOULD copy profile entries verbatim; narrowing is allowed, widening is not. A git or gh token in a skill's allowed-tools that appears in no profile is reported for review.

section.name: Glossary Terms: Adding One
section.t: SDS-K-050 (MUST, MACHINE) Glossary rows are term | definition | do-not-use.
SDS-K-051 (SHOULD, REVIEW) Each row SHOULD cite the section of this specification that fixes the concept.

section.name: The Eval Template
section.t: SDS-K-060 (MUST, MACHINE) kit/evals/TEMPLATE.eval.yaml defines the row schema every skill's eval file follows: name, optional input, and expected with kind (success, failure, or not-applicable), optional shape, failureCode, reason, and assertions. Per-skill conformance is checked by .

section.name: The Linter
section.t: SDS-K-070 (MUST, MACHINE) kit/scripts/lint-skill.py <skill-dir> or --all skills/ MUST exit 0 only when every MUST+MACHINE rule passes, exit 1 on any such failure, and exit 2 on usage or I/O error. It prints one finding per line as <ID> <LEVEL> <root-relative path>[:line] <message>, prints REVIEW rules as a trailing checklist, and with --json emits a finding-list instance validating against kit/shapes/finding-list.schema.json.
SDS-K-071 (MUST, REVIEW) The linter's MACHINE rule table (--rules) MUST equal the MACHINE subset of .

section.name: The Eval Runner
section.t: SDS-K-072 (MUST, REVIEW) kit/scripts/run-evals.py <skill-dir> or --all skills/ MUST run each generator () and then every row of the eval table that carries input.command, from the skill directory (), and judge it by expected.kind: success requires exit 0 and, when expected.shape names a registered Shape and the output is JSON, validation against that Shape's schema (the artifact may sit inside a Command Skill's dry-run envelope); failure requires a non-zero exit and the row's failureCode on stderr; not-applicable rows are skipped. It MUST NOT run the smoke section after the table (). It exits 0 only when every executed row passed. Prose assertions are for the reviewer; the runner does not evaluate them.

section.name: Package Layout
section.t: SDS-S-001 (MUST, MACHINE) SKILL.md MUST exist at the skill root.
SDS-S-002 (MUST, MACHINE) Exactly one evals/<name>.eval.yaml MUST exist.
SDS-S-003 (MUST, MACHINE) The directory name MUST equal the frontmatter name.
SDS-S-004 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Only scripts/, references/, assets/, and evals/ SHOULD appear beside SKILL.md.
SDS-S-005 (MAY, MACHINE) An empty scripts/, references/, or assets/ directory is reported.

section.name: Frontmatter
section.t: SDS-S-010 (MUST, MACHINE) Only the Base Spec keys name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, and allowed-tools MUST appear at the frontmatter top level.
SDS-S-011 (MUST, MACHINE) name MUST match ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and be at most 64 characters.
SDS-S-012 (MUST, MACHINE) description MUST be 1 to 1024 characters.

SDS-S-013 (SHOULD, MACHINE) description SHOULD contain a trigger phrase ("Use when" or equivalent) and the specific keywords a task would contain. Write it last, after the body, so it describes real triggers rather than summarizing the draft.
SDS-S-014 (SHOULD, MACHINE) license SHOULD be set explicitly; the family default is Apache-2.0, and a different value is reported for information.

SDS-S-015 (MUST, MACHINE) compatibility, when present, MUST be at most 500 characters and name concrete requirements. It MUST be present when effect-tier is external-read-only or higher, and SHOULD be omitted when the skill needs nothing beyond a host that supports Agent Skills.
SDS-S-016 (MUST, MACHINE) metadata MUST be a map of string values containing exactly the seven keys family, effect-tier, idempotent, tier, shape-out, shape-in, and version.
section.sourcecode: metadata: family: dev-skills-suite effect-tier: external-read-only idempotent: "true" tier: pillar shape-out: finding-list shape-in: freeform version: "0.1.0"
section.t: SDS-S-017 (MUST, MACHINE) effect-tier MUST be one of the six rung names in .
SDS-S-018 (MUST, MACHINE) idempotent MUST be the YAML string "true" or "false" (Base Spec metadata is string-to-string; an unquoted boolean is nonconformant).
SDS-S-019 (MUST, MACHINE) tier MUST be pillar or situational.
SDS-S-020 (MUST, MACHINE) Any skill whose Procedure reaches rung 2 or above and invokes any tool or bundled script MUST declare allowed-tools as a single string.

SDS-S-021 (MUST, MACHINE) allowed-tools has two sources and only two: entries copied verbatim from a shared profile (), and one inline entry per shipped script of the form Bash(python3 scripts/<file>:*). Script entries MUST reference files that exist under scripts/ and nothing outside it.
SDS-S-022 (MUST, MACHINE) allowed-tools MUST NOT contain a bare interpreter or wildcard ().

SDS-S-023 (MUST, MACHINE) allowed-tools MUST NOT contain a forbidden-always operation at any rung, a forbidden-below-5 operation below rung 5 (), or, below rung 4, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, git checkout -b, or git stash.
SDS-S-024 (MUST, REVIEW) Write and Edit tools MUST appear only in Command Skills, and only for the checkpoint record or the skill's declared output location.

SDS-S-025 (MUST, MACHINE) Body sections MUST match the rung's kind: rung 3 or lower has no Confirm, Act, or Communicate heading; rung 4 or higher has an Act heading; rung 5 or higher has a Confirm heading that precedes Act.
SDS-S-026 (MUST, MACHINE) shape-out and each value of shape-in (a name or a comma-separated list) MUST be a registered Shape or freeform.
SDS-S-027 (MUST, MACHINE) version MUST be semver ().
SDS-S-028 (MUST, MACHINE) family MUST equal the registry's family.

section.name: Section Order
section.t: SDS-S-030 (MUST, MACHINE) The SKILL.md body MUST contain exactly these H2 sections, in this order, none empty: When to use, When not to use, @requires, Instructions, @returns, @throws, @example. The only additional H2 sections permitted are @see and @deprecated, referencing a superseding skill (). The tag vocabulary follows established docstring conventions .
SDS-S-043 (SHOULD, MACHINE) The first heading SHOULD be # <name>.

SDS-S-031 (MUST, MACHINE) H3 headings under Instructions MUST be stage-vocabulary names (). A Query Skill MUST have Gather, Analyze, and Synthesize; Filter and Classify MAY be omitted entirely. A Command Skill MUST have Gather, Analyze, Decide, Act, Communicate, and Persist, plus Confirm (optional at rung 4, required at rungs 5 and 6). Required stages MUST appear as a subsequence of the canonical order.
SDS-S-032 (MUST, MACHINE) A required heading that does not apply MUST be retained with a body whose first line is N/A — <reason>; a missing section is indistinguishable from a forgotten one.
SDS-S-033 (MUST, MACHINE) No template residue ([FILL, skill-name-here, [Write this LAST) MUST remain.

SDS-S-034 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Instructions SHOULD be second-person imperative, one checkable action per sentence, and MUST NOT use marketing language (powerful, seamless, comprehensive, robust, cutting-edge).
SDS-S-035 (MUST, MACHINE) SKILL.md MUST be under 500 lines; 400 or more is a warning. Move depth to references/ rather than trimming required sections.
SDS-S-036 (MUST, MACHINE) Each @requires bullet MUST begin REQUIRED: or OPTIONAL:; an OPTIONAL: bullet MUST carry (default: ...) unless it is exactly OPTIONAL: none.
SDS-S-037 (MUST, MACHINE) At least one REQUIRED input MUST be declared; more than five is reported as a warning to split the skill ().
SDS-S-038 (MUST, MACHINE) @returns MUST contain Shape: `<shape-out>` and, for a registered Shape, the literal kit/shapes/<shape-out>.schema.json.

SDS-S-039 (MUST, MACHINE) @throws MUST have at least one bullet of the form - `kebab-code`: ...; codes MUST be unique; every failureCode in the eval file MUST be a declared code; a skill at rung 5 or higher SHOULD declare a declined-confirmation code.

section.name: Conditional Command Skills
section.t: SDS-S-041 (MUST, MACHINE) A Command Skill MAY declare a conditional Act path. If it does, Decide MUST contain a bold branch of the form **If <condition>: stop here.** returning the artifact; the Confirm and Act sections MUST begin Only reached when <condition>.; @returns MUST describe both paths; and @throws MUST include the declined-confirmation code.
SDS-S-042 (MUST, REVIEW) The Act-less path MUST NOT mutate anything; on that path the invocation behaves as a Query Skill.

section.name: Confirm, Act, and Checkpoint
section.t: SDS-S-050 (MUST, MACHINE) A rung-5 Confirm section MUST cite kit/shared/gates/medium.md; a rung-6 Confirm section MUST cite kit/shared/gates/high.md; Confirm MUST precede Act.

SDS-S-051 (MUST, MACHINE) A rung-5 or rung-6 Act MUST be issued as a direct, unwrapped tool call after Confirm. It MUST NOT be delegated to a bundled script, because pre-approving the script pre-approves the mutation and silently bypasses the gate. A script in a skill at rung 5 or higher MUST NOT invoke a mutating command via a subprocess.
SDS-S-052 (MUST, REVIEW) Act MUST state the check-before-act no-op skip explicitly ().

SDS-S-053 (MUST, MACHINE) A rung-4-or-higher Act section MUST contain a **Checkpoint** label describing the two-phase record of : written with status: pending before the mutating call, updated to status: completed immediately after it succeeds. A resumed invocation reading pending MUST treat the step as possibly applied and check-before-act; reading completed MUST skip the step. Single-step Command Skills MUST checkpoint: the pending record is what makes the compensating action executable.
SDS-S-054 (MUST, MACHINE) A rung-4-or-higher Act section MUST contain a **Compensating action** label for each mutating step ().
SDS-S-055 (SHOULD, REVIEW) A skill with one mutating step SHOULD write its checkpoint inline; a skill with two or more SHOULD use scripts/checkpoint.py.

SDS-S-056 (SHOULD, REVIEW) A mutating call in an Act section SHOULD name its target explicitly — the repository (-R owner/repo), the branch (--head), the state directory (--state-dir) — rather than relying on the working directory, and the Act's commands SHOULD all run from the skill directory. Changing directory between the pending record, the mutation, and the completed record breaks the skill-relative script paths of and leaves a pending record after a successful mutation; observed in a live run of release-publisher.

section.name: scripts/
section.t: SDS-S-060 (MUST, REVIEW) A sub-step MUST be a script when it is deterministic, mechanical, and requires no interpretation of ambiguous input (the toil test ): parsing a real grammar, calling an external system and normalizing its response, or translating one format to another (an Adapter).
SDS-S-061 (MUST, REVIEW) Analyze, Classify, and Decide MUST NOT live in a script; a script cannot exercise judgment.

SDS-S-062 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Files under scripts/ SHOULD be snake_case verb-noun names (parse_manifest.py); an Adapter names both sides (osv_to_finding.py). This rule does not apply to fixture generators under evals/fixtures/.

SDS-S-063 (MUST, MACHINE) Every script MUST begin with a shebang and carry a module docstring (or a leading comment block for shell); it prints JSON to stdout, exits 0 with an empty instance on empty input, and exits 1 with an ERROR: line on stderr on failure (the presence of error handling is checked as a warning).
SDS-S-064 (MUST, REVIEW) Any dependency beyond the standard library MUST be named in the script's docstring and in compatibility.
SDS-S-065 (SHOULD, MACHINE) A script that calls an external system SHOULD expose a --<thing>-file flag substituting a fixture for the live call, so that evals exercise the same code path offline.
SDS-S-066 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Scripts SHOULD carry the owner execute bit.
SDS-S-067 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Every file under scripts/ SHOULD be referenced from SKILL.md.

section.name: references/
section.t: SDS-S-070 (MUST, REVIEW) Content needed on every invocation MUST live in SKILL.md; content needed only sometimes MUST live under references/, loaded on demand.
SDS-S-071 (SHOULD, MACHINE) A file under references/ SHOULD NOT link to another file under references/ (one level deep).
SDS-S-072 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Each SKILL.md pointer to references/ SHOULD be phrased as a condition ("If unsure why X, consult ..."), not a blanket instruction.
SDS-S-073 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Every file under references/ SHOULD be linked from SKILL.md.

section.name: assets/
section.t: SDS-S-080 (MUST, MACHINE) assets/ MUST NOT contain a copy of a family Shape schema; reference kit/shapes/ directly.
SDS-S-081 (MUST, MACHINE) Every assets/ file the Procedure reads MUST be named in @requires or Instructions; it is a declared input for hermeticity ().
SDS-S-082 (MUST, REVIEW) Per-installation configuration MUST be injected via assets/, never by forking ().

section.name: evals/ and Fixtures
section.t: SDS-S-090 (MUST, MACHINE) The eval file MUST parse; skill MUST equal name; rows MUST be non-empty with unique names; each expected.kind MUST be success, failure, or not-applicable; a not-applicable row MUST carry a non-empty reason; a failure row MUST carry failureCode; any YAML document after the first MUST be empty (the smoke section is comments).
SDS-S-091 (SHOULD, MACHINE) A success row SHOULD carry at least one assertion about content or shape and, for a registered Shape, a shape field. "Runs without erroring" is not a passing eval.

SDS-S-092 (MUST, MACHINE) For a skill at rung 3 or higher, no required row MUST invoke a live external system (curl, wget, http://, https://, gh api, pip install, npm install). Live checks live after the --- document separator as a non-blocking smoke test asserting shape only, never specific content, because the content of an open-world system changes for reasons unrelated to the skill's correctness.

SDS-S-093 (SHOULD, MACHINE) A frozen recording of a real external response SHOULD be named evals/fixtures/frozen-<source>-<what>.json — or the source's native text extension (.txt, .log, .yaml, .xml, .md) when the response is not JSON, such as a recorded git log — captured once and never refreshed by the evals.

SDS-S-094 (MUST, MACHINE) A row named fixed-point MUST exist. It is a success row iff shape-out equals shape-in and both are registered Shapes (); otherwise it is not-applicable with the reason stated.

SDS-S-095 (MUST, MACHINE) A row named mutation-fixture MUST exist. It is a success row referencing an evals/fixtures/ path with a deliberately planted instance of what the skill detects iff shape-out is finding-list; otherwise it is not-applicable with the reason stated.

SDS-S-096 (MUST, MACHINE) Static fixtures live in evals/fixtures/<case>/, with .gitkeep marking an intentionally empty case. A fixture that is itself a version-control repository MUST NOT be checked in; it MUST be produced by an executable, idempotent evals/fixtures/build-<name>.sh whose output directory is listed in evals/fixtures/.gitignore. Any nested .git under fixtures MUST be ignored. Every fixture path a row references MUST exist or be generated.
SDS-S-097 (SHOULD, MACHINE) Every fixture file SHOULD be referenced by a row or by the smoke section.
SDS-S-098 (MUST, MACHINE) Rows MUST reference only paths inside the skill directory or under kit/; absolute paths and ~ are reported as non-hermetic.

SDS-S-099 (MUST, MACHINE) The table MUST contain a success row named happy-path*; at least two boundary-* rows, one a success on empty/zero/minimal input and one a failure on malformed/invalid/missing input; and a row named contract-with-* (), which MAY be not-applicable with a reason. Evals follow the table-driven convention .

section.name: Runtime State
section.t: SDS-S-100 (MUST, MACHINE) A Command Skill's runtime state MUST live at <family-root>/.skills-state/<name>/<key>.json, where <key> uniquely identifies the invocation (a PR number, a branch, a migration id); the skill's Act section names this path. Referencing another skill's state directory is an error. The family root is the root of the skill family's own checkout, not of the repository the skill is operating on: when a skill runs inside some other repository (the normal case for a GitHub-operating skill), its state still lives under the family's .skills-state/, and a bundled checkpoint script MUST accept an explicit state directory for exactly that situation rather than assuming the working directory is inside the family.
SDS-S-101 (MUST, REVIEW) The checkpoint record MUST have the following form.
section.sourcecode: { "key": "<invocation key>", "step": "<mutating step name>", "status": "pending" | "completed", "startedAt": "<ISO-8601>", "preState": { ... }, "compensatingAction": "<what undoes this step>", "postState": { ... } // present only when completed }

section.name: Validation Gate
section.t: SDS-S-110 (MUST, REVIEW) A skill is done only when: (0) the linter passes with no errors; (1) metadata matches what the Procedure actually does; (2) an example artifact validates against its Shape's schema; (3) every eval row passes under the eval runner (), including the mutation fixture and fixed-point row where required, and its prose assertions hold against the actual output; and (4) the glossary check passes. If any fails, fix the skill — not the eval, and not the glossary.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This specification is, in large part, a security specification, and together with is its core normative content. The following risks are called out explicitly:

ul.li: Declared hints (Effect Ladder rung, MCP annotations, allowed-tools) are self-reported and MUST be treated as untrusted absent a trusted source (). A mis-declared rung is a directly exploitable path to bypassing confirmation.
A pre-approved script that performs a mutation is a bypassed gate (): the host approves "run this script," and the script, not the model's next tool call, performs the effect.

Content gathered from an open-world source during a Query stage may later inform a Decide or Act stage. It MUST be treated as data, not instruction; a Procedure MUST NOT follow directives inside gathered content.
Fixtures, including frozen recordings of external responses, are untrusted data of the same kind and MUST NOT be executed or followed as instruction.
Bundled scripts/ are executable code with the supply-chain risk of any third-party code; a family SHOULD review and pin them like a dependency.
Overly broad allowed-tools scoping does not merely fail to add safety; it suppresses the host's own confirmation mechanism from engaging.
Compensating actions are themselves effects and MUST meet the same confirmation requirements as the action they undo when they sit at rung 5 or above.

section.name: Registry Considerations
section.t: This specification establishes the following registries, each maintained by a family for itself:

dl.dd: new entries require a Standards-First check (), a machine-checkable schema (), and a defined zero-entry form (); changes follow .
one entry per skill, planned or built, validated against its schema; the only source for generated indexes.
six fixed rungs. A family MUST NOT reorder them but MAY define sub-tiers within a rung, provided the six-rung classification remains derivable.
the list of operations no profile may pre-approve; a family MAY extend it but MUST NOT remove an entry.
identifiers are permanent ().

section.name: Worked Examples
section.t: Ten skills are maintained as conformance examples and are the standing test subjects of the linter; the registry (kit/registry/marketplace.json) and the generated index (README.md) list them. Each was chosen to exercise a part of this specification the others do not:

ul.li: skills/dependency-audit/ — Query, rung 3, finding-list: bundled scripts (parser, external query with an injectable fixture flag, Adapter), an on-demand reference file, a frozen external recording in its evals.

skills/pr-description-writer/ — Command, rung 5, freeform: the Confirm gate, the two-phase checkpoint, a compensating action, an unwrapped rung-5 Act, a conditional Act path, a generated (not checked-in) version-control fixture.

skills/pr-lifecycle-manager/ — Command, rung 6, decision-doc in, status-report out: an orchestrator with no Analyze logic of its own (SDS-C-060), a multi-step Act with a compensating action per step, the high gate re-shown before the irreversible step, and scripts/checkpoint.py; validated by a live open-verify-merge run against a real repository.

skills/sync-strategy-advisor/ — Query, rung 2, decision-doc: a fully offline git-state assessment over a generated bare-origin-plus-clone fixture, with the one judgment a script cannot make (is the branch shared) left to Analyze.
skills/adr-writer/ — Command, rung 4, decision-doc: an Act without a mandatory gate, MADR rendering, and immutability with supersession (SDS-C-034).
skills/tech-debt-inventory/ — Query, rung 1, finding-list: a local scanner with the mandatory mutation-fixture row and a reference loaded only on demand.
skills/flaky-test-triage/ — Query, rung 2, finding-list: JUnit XML as the interchange standard, mechanical evidence separated from a three-way classification that may answer "undetermined".
skills/incident-postmortem/ — Command, rung 4, status-report: a judgment-heavy skill whose script checks completeness and flags blaming language as warnings, never failures; two on-demand references.
skills/performance-budget-check/ — Query, rung 1, finding-list: Lighthouse CI budget.json as the standard input, regressions reported even within budget.
skills/api-doc-writer/ — Command, rung 4, freeform: the first use of assets/ (a per-skill intermediate schema, SDS-S-080) and an explicit undocumented marker in place of invented behavior.

section.t: The software-development catalog described in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-dev-skills-suite-design.md is the first applied instance of this specification; its clusters, shape choices, and rung assignments are one domain's answer to the Standards-First Rule, not part of this specification.

section.name: Rule Index
section.t: Every rule in this document, in identifier order. Levels are MUST, SHOULD, or MAY; tags are MACHINE, REVIEW, or ADVISORY (). The linter's --rules output is diffed against the MACHINE rows of this table.

section.name: Change Log
section.t: 1.0-draft, revision 04 (2026-09-06): Adds the eval runner. SDS-K-001 now requires kit/scripts/run-evals.py (MACHINE rule changed; linter updated in the same change). New SDS-K-072 (MUST, REVIEW): the runner's contract — generators first, then every row with a command, judged by expected.kind, exit code, failureCode on stderr, and Shape validation; never the smoke section. New SDS-F-054 (SHOULD, ADVISORY): the family runs its validation gate in continuous integration. SDS-S-110 now cites the runner. Introduced when the first family-wide run of the runner found fifteen rows the linter could not see — folded commands, undocumented failure codes on stderr, one borrowed code, one mislabelled intermediate — all fixed in the skills.

1.0-draft, revision 03 (2026-09-06): Adds SDS-K-023 (SHOULD, REVIEW): a family carries a machine check that each registered Shape stays backward compatible with its copy at the last tag, the concrete form of SDS-F-051's MAJOR-change review — introduced when json-schema-compat-check made it a one-row eval against frozen copies of the four shapes at v1.0.0-draft. One REVIEW rule added to Appendix B; no MACHINE rule changed. Editorial: SDS-S-093 admits a native text extension for a frozen recording that is not JSON (a git log shared by changelog-writer and commit-message-lint).

1.0-draft, revision 02 (2026-09-06): Folds in what building the twenty-eight situational skills and two more live runs taught. SDS-F-061 now exempts a glossary term that is part of a proper noun or an identifier (the GitHub cluster's own nouns — issue, Projects, board item — were unspeakable under the bare heuristic; the glossary gained rows for them). SDS-F-031 now lets a consumer-driven contract row run another skill's script by its family-root-relative path, because the strongest contract is the real consumer (rfc-writer renders, then design-doc-review's own script must find nothing). New SDS-S-056 (SHOULD, REVIEW): a mutating call names its target explicitly rather than relying on the working directory. The linter's heuristics changed to match; one REVIEW rule was added to Appendix B; no MACHINE rule was added or removed.

1.0-draft, editorial (2026-09-06): SDS-S-100 now states that the family root is the skill family's own checkout, not the repository a skill operates on, and that a bundled checkpoint script must accept an explicit state directory — observed while driving pr-lifecycle-manager against a separate repository. No rule was added, removed, or re-tagged; Appendix B is unchanged.

1.0-draft (2026-09-05): Restructured top to bottom into Part 0 (core model), Part I (family and repository), Part II (kit), and Part III (skill anatomy); every normative rule now carries a permanent identifier and a MACHINE/REVIEW/ADVISORY tag, indexed in Appendix B; added the conformance linter contract. Resolved nine drift findings against the kit and the two worked skills: (1) the fixed-point law is gated on a registered shape-out equal to shape-in, not on idempotent; (2) checkpointing is two-phase — a pending record written before the mutating call, updated to completed after — and single-step Command Skills must checkpoint; (3) metadata has exactly seven string keys; (4) allowed-tools is required by rung, not kind, with two declared sources; (5) tier vocabulary is pillar / situational; (6) a conditional Act path is a permitted Command form with Confirm/Act headings retained and Communicate/ Persist always present; (7) the registry is kit/registry/marketplace.json with required shape-in/shape-out, status, and a top-level sds version (the former example registry file name is retired); (8) all cross-references are family-root-relative; (9) fixtures have a defined layout with generated repositories, frozen recordings, and a no-live-call rule for open-world stages. Also added: the checkpoint state path, the prohibition on wrapping a rung-5/6 Act in a pre-approved script, script and reference conventions, the long-parameter-list rule, and the validation gate.
0.3 (2026-09-05): Rebuilt in xml2rfc version 3 (RFC 7991) vocabulary in place of the plain-text RFC-style draft. No normative changes from 0.2.

0.2 (2026-09-05): Rebuilt as an RFC-structured document: added formal Terminology, Security Considerations, and Registry Considerations sections; added full Normative/ Informative References with verified citations for MCP tool annotations, SARIF, OSV, SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962:2021), CycloneDX (ECMA-424), and MADR (v4.0.0); formalized the composition laws, contracts, and effect ladder with MUST/SHOULD/MAY language throughout.
0.1 (2026-09-05): Initial high-level draft.
